- Balance sheet is debt-free as at Mar-26 on the deck's own lines: non-current Borrowings Rs 488.14 Mn (Mar-24) to 0 (Mar-25) to 0 (Mar-26); Short term Borrowings Rs 279.11 Mn (Mar-24) to Rs 265.89 Mn (Mar-25) to 0 (Mar-26).

- Management frames the philosophy as "pursuing disciplined growth opportunities. Backed by a strong balance sheet, a healthy pipeline, and differentiated technology"; no dividend or buyback policy is stated anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Proprietary handwriting-recognition and marking capability built on multi-model orchestration - vision transformers for spatial understanding of handwritten layout, assessment-specific NLP models, weighted ensembles, and confidence scoring with anomaly detection that routes ambiguous regions to human review
- Displaces an entrenched manual workflow - the handwritten script evaluation market is currently dominated by labor-intensive manual marking processes, and Excelsoft's technology fundamentally displaces this workflow for examination boards, awarding bodies and educational institutions
- Responsible-AI framework treated as a commercial differentiator rather than compliance - explainable marking decisions, fairness audits for algorithmic bias across demographic groups, privacy by design, and detailed logs of all AI-powered decisions to meet the transparency and governance standards high-stakes assessment boards require
- Data custody as a trust moat - all customer data and assessment scripts remain within Excelsoft's secure, proprietary infrastructure; the Company does not train models on customer data without explicit consent, nor share assessment data with external AI providers
- Owned AI compute - an in-house GPU environment at Mysore (NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada workstations, plus capacity at a peered partner data centre) lets customer workloads run on dedicated, ring-fenced environments and supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment for customers with strict data-residency obligations
- Proprietary internal AI leverage - Excelsoft GPT is fine-tuned on the Company's own codebase, technical documentation, domain knowledge and processes, so it provides significantly more valuable assistance than generic LLMs
- Engineering cost advantage - AI-assisted schema redesign delivered a 60% reduction in database footprint while maintaining or improving query performance, translating to lower infrastructure costs and improved scalability
- Long-tenured customer relationships - customers span more than 20 countries and many relationships have endured for over a decade, a durable switching-cost signal in high-stakes assessment
- Emerging high-margin AI service line - dedicated GPU hardware-as-a-service, managed model deployment and fine-tuning services position Excelsoft as a strategic AI partner rather than merely a SaaS vendor
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Information-security and data-privacy exposure across a trust-intensive assessment platform — The governance sustainability strategy is framed around 'Strengthen Trust - Embed ESG risk in enterprise risk management; reinforce cybersecurity, ISO 27001 readiness, and DPDP Act alignment', indicating these controls are still being built out. High-stakes examination data is the Company's core custodial asset, so a breach is a direct threat to customer trust and contract renewal.
- Responsible-AI risk — bias, transparency and explainability in AI-assisted assessment — The Company lists 'Build Responsible Products — Reinforce product quality, customer safety, and responsible AI principles covering bias, transparency, and explainability' as a sustainability priority. Because AI is embedded in marking and proctoring workflows for regulated awarding bodies, an unexplainable or biased AI decision is both a regulatory and a reputational risk.
- Key-management transition and leadership continuity — The Board's Report records that Subramaniam Ravi, CFO, tendered his resignation vide letter dated 01 June, 2026 with effect from close of business on 31 August, 2026. A CFO vacancy shortly after listing is a continuity and financial-controls watch item.
- Enterprise risk oversight rests on a voluntary, newly constituted committee — The Company did not fall within the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation as on 31 December, 2025 and so was not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee; the Board constituted it voluntarily. Risk governance is therefore not yet regulator-mandated and is only in its first cycle.
- Reduced mandatory ESG disclosure — BRSR exemption taken for FY 2025-26 — Being outside the top 1,000 listed entities, the Company is exempt from mandatory BRSR under Regulation 34(2)(f) of the SEBI LODR and 'has opted not to map voluntary disclosures for the current period', which limits externally comparable, assured ESG and responsible-business-conduct data.
- Global macroeconomic and geopolitical volatility — MD&A states the balance of risks has shifted to the downside, driven by geopolitical uncertainty, commodity price volatility and evolving financial conditions, following the escalation of Middle East tensions, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude exceeding USD 120 per barrel. Growth forecasts were downgraded to approximately 2.9% and supply chains remained under inflationary pressure — relevant to a business selling into government and institutional budgets worldwide.
- People risk — employee wellbeing, burnout and dependence on scarce engineering talent — 'Employee wellbeing and burnout prevention' is named as a material social sustainability priority, alongside upskilling, career pathways and measurable DEI goals. The Company's competitive position rests on engineering and applied-AI talent, making attrition and burnout a structural constraint.
- Value-chain and supply-chain conduct risk — 'Responsible supply chain management' and 'Responsible lobbying and public policy' are listed as material governance issues, with a stated intent to deploy a supplier code and ESG due diligence — indicating these controls are being built rather than already in place.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Shift decisively to an AI-first operating model with a full-stack approach to Artificial Intelligence — building capability at every layer of the stack: compute infrastructure, foundation models, fine-tuning, orchestration, applications and domain adaptation
- Own the AI compute layer — procure NVIDIA A6000 GPUs and run an in-house GPU environment at Mysore (plus RTX 6000 Ada workstations and peered partner data-centre capacity) so customer AI workloads run on dedicated, ring-fenced environments and support on-premise and air-gapped deployment for data-residency-bound customers
- Self-host open-weight large language models on owned infrastructure for the most sensitive and highest-volume workloads, while evaluating and deploying a portfolio of commercial and open-weight models by risk and volume profile — explicitly framed as import substitution and data sovereignty
- Democratise AI internally through Excelsoft GPT, extending access beyond engineering to non-technical teams and interns to build organisation-wide fluency rather than isolated pockets of expertise
- Institutionalise AI-driven engineering and operate a disciplined innovation funnel — a structured idea-to-product pipeline taking ideas through prototyping and customer piloting before commercial launch
- Strengthen governance of technology adoption — model selection, validation, risk controls, explainability, security, customer isolation and human oversight, formalised through an AI Feature Lifecycle Checklist and a Corporate AI Usage Policy that AI features pass before reaching a customer
- Absorb global learning and assessment interoperability and digital accessibility standards so platforms interoperate with customer ecosystems and meet regulator and awarding-body expectations
- Expand the four-vertical platform portfolio (Education Technology Services, Assessment & Proctoring, Learning & Student Success, Learning Design & Content) and deepen presence in vocational assessment and public-sector examinations
- Deepen AI capability inside the Saras platform, with the handwriting recognition and marking engine positioned as the lever for faster, more accurate and fairer evaluation of handwritten scripts at scale
- Maintain governance discipline as a newly listed company, with continued focus on cybersecurity, data privacy, business continuity and the responsible use of AI
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Excelsoft's expansion in FY 2025-26 was platform and compute build-out rather than plant capacity. The Company has built proprietary, full-stack AI capability including GPU-based computing, with its multi-LLM handwriting-recognition architecture (98.6% accuracy) deployed on in-house GPU infrastructure. Intangible assets under development reflect ongoing R&D capitalisation for next-generation product development, including AI-powered assessment tools. On the facilities side, a purchase order was released to M/s RAY ENERGY SOLUTIONS, Mysore (PO# MYS-PO-02635, dated 02 March, 2026) for a 150 kWp rooftop solar photovoltaic plant, which is completed and expected to be commissioned during FY 2026-27; 110 CFL bulbs were also replaced with LED lights. Funding comes from the November 2025 IPO: the Fresh Issue proceeds of INR 180 Crore are being utilised towards capital expenditure requirements, and management states its net cash position, inclusive of IPO proceeds, provides funding for planned capital expenditure, infrastructure upgrades and strategic acquisitions, with no dividend recommended for FY26 so profits are retained for growth. Commercial expansion is contract- and geography-led: a joint R&D and e-marking collaboration with AQA (UK) with revenue expected to commence from Q1 FY27 and scale as examination volumes migrate to Excelsoft's platforms; selection (with ASEAMETRICS) to power the Civil Service Digital Examination (CSC DeX) in the Philippines from 2026, a multi-year engagement supporting over 300,000 candidates annually; and a multi-year VTCT Skills (UK) engagement deploying the next-generation SARAS eTesting platform for 300,000 vocational and technical examinations annually. Management is actively pursuing opportunities in Egypt, France, Italy, Brazil and additional Southeast Asian markets, expects the AI handwritten-script engine to process up to 12 million scripts annually within 3-5 years, and plans to lift product revenue contribution from 40% currently to 50% by FY29.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global shift from paper to digital examinations, the rising demand for skilling and certification, and the emergence of AI-enabled learning ecosystems are opening opportunities well suited to the Company's strengths
- Digital transformation of high-stakes assessment — governments, professional bodies and awarding organisations are transitioning from paper-based to digital formats, creating demand for secure, scalable, AI-enabled assessment platforms across the full examination lifecycle
- AI integration across the learning lifecycle is reshaping every stage from AI-assisted item authoring and intelligent proctoring to automated marking, predictive learner analytics and personalised learning pathways
- Growth of vocational and skills-based assessments, particularly in the UK, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, driving demand for platforms that assess trade skills and professional competencies at scale
- Vertical SaaS as the dominant enterprise model — domain-specialised platforms are displacing generic horizontal solutions, with customers preferring providers with deep domain knowledge and trusted implementation records
- Rise of AI-powered handwritten script evaluation as a high-value emerging opportunity
- Learning experience platforms gaining wider adoption and upskilling/reskilling becoming business priorities, with organisations adopting modular, on-demand and lifelong learning models
- Structural market growth: Global Learning & Development from USD 390.20 Bn (2024) to USD 587.61 Bn (2030) at 7.06% CAGR, and Global Assessment & Proctoring from USD 10.83 Bn to USD 21.26 Bn at 11.90% CAGR (Arizton)
- India's continued government emphasis on infrastructure investment, digital public infrastructure, skilling and education reform is expected to sustain favourable long-term growth conditions for the education technology sector and the broader digital services ecosystem
- Downside macro risk — MD&A notes the balance of risks has shifted to the downside on geopolitical uncertainty, commodity price volatility and evolving financial conditions, with global growth forecasts downgraded to approximately 2.9%
- Both Education Technology Services and Assessment & Proctoring gained momentum, supported by deeper product capability and a stronger global footprint
- One of the largest mandates in the Company's history with a leading examination body in the United Kingdom, supporting digital assessment at national scale
- Engagement with VTCT Skills, strengthening presence in vocational assessment
- Work with the Civil Service Commission of the Philippines, reinforcing credibility in the public sector
- Customers across more than 20 countries, with many relationships that have endured for over a decade
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Excelsoft combines proprietary learning and assessment platforms with specialist technology and content services, spanning content creation and learning delivery through digital assessment, remote proctoring, student success and the modernisation of learning environments. It sells across four business verticals — Education Technology Services, Assessment and Proctoring Solutions, Learning & Student Success Solutions, and Learning Design & Content Solutions — to examination boards, awarding bodies, government examination authorities, publishers, schools, higher-education institutions and enterprises. During FY 2025-26 the Company shifted to an AI-first operating model, building a full-stack AI capability across compute infrastructure, foundation models, fine-tuning, orchestration, applications and domain adaptation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global shift from paper to digital examinations, the rising demand for skilling and certification, and the emergence of AI-enabled learning ecosystems are opening opportunities well suited to the Company's strengths
- Digital transformation of high-stakes assessment — governments, professional bodies and awarding organisations are transitioning from paper-based to digital formats, creating demand for secure, scalable, AI-enabled assessment platforms across the full examination lifecycle
- AI integration across the learning lifecycle is reshaping every stage from AI-assisted item authoring and intelligent proctoring to automated marking, predictive learner analytics and personalised learning pathways
- Growth of vocational and skills-based assessments, particularly in the UK, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, driving demand for platforms that assess trade skills and professional competencies at scale
- Vertical SaaS as the dominant enterprise model — domain-specialised platforms are displacing generic horizontal solutions, with customers preferring providers with deep domain knowledge and trusted implementation records
- Rise of AI-powered handwritten script evaluation as a high-value emerging opportunity
- Learning experience platforms gaining wider adoption and upskilling/reskilling becoming business priorities, with organisations adopting modular, on-demand and lifelong learning models
- Structural market growth: Global Learning & Development from USD 390.20 Bn (2024) to USD 587.61 Bn (2030) at 7.06% CAGR, and Global Assessment & Proctoring from USD 10.83 Bn to USD 21.26 Bn at 11.90% CAGR (Arizton)
- India's continued government emphasis on infrastructure investment, digital public infrastructure, skilling and education reform is expected to sustain favourable long-term growth conditions for the education technology sector and the broader digital services ecosystem
- Downside macro risk — MD&A notes the balance of risks has shifted to the downside on geopolitical uncertainty, commodity price volatility and evolving financial conditions, with global growth forecasts downgraded to approximately 2.9%
- Both Education Technology Services and Assessment & Proctoring gained momentum, supported by deeper product capability and a stronger global footprint
- One of the largest mandates in the Company's history with a leading examination body in the United Kingdom, supporting digital assessment at national scale
- Engagement with VTCT Skills, strengthening presence in vocational assessment
- Work with the Civil Service Commission of the Philippines, reinforcing credibility in the public sector
- Customers across more than 20 countries, with many relationships that have endured for over a decade

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Excelsoft's expansion in FY 2025-26 was platform and compute build-out rather than plant capacity. The Company has built proprietary, full-stack AI capability including GPU-based computing, with its multi-LLM handwriting-recognition architecture (98.6% accuracy) deployed on in-house GPU infrastructure. Intangible assets under development reflect ongoing R&D capitalisation for next-generation product development, including AI-powered assessment tools. On the facilities side, a purchase order was released to M/s RAY ENERGY SOLUTIONS, Mysore (PO# MYS-PO-02635, dated 02 March, 2026) for a 150 kWp rooftop solar photovoltaic plant, which is completed and expected to be commissioned during FY 2026-27; 110 CFL bulbs were also replaced with LED lights. Funding comes from the November 2025 IPO: the Fresh Issue proceeds of INR 180 Crore are being utilised towards capital expenditure requirements, and management states its net cash position, inclusive of IPO proceeds, provides funding for planned capital expenditure, infrastructure upgrades and strategic acquisitions, with no dividend recommended for FY26 so profits are retained for growth. Commercial expansion is contract- and geography-led: a joint R&D and e-marking collaboration with AQA (UK) with revenue expected to commence from Q1 FY27 and scale as examination volumes migrate to Excelsoft's platforms; selection (with ASEAMETRICS) to power the Civil Service Digital Examination (CSC DeX) in the Philippines from 2026, a multi-year engagement supporting over 300,000 candidates annually; and a multi-year VTCT Skills (UK) engagement deploying the next-generation SARAS eTesting platform for 300,000 vocational and technical examinations annually. Management is actively pursuing opportunities in Egypt, France, Italy, Brazil and additional Southeast Asian markets, expects the AI handwritten-script engine to process up to 12 million scripts annually within 3-5 years, and plans to lift product revenue contribution from 40% currently to 50% by FY29.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Proprietary handwriting-recognition and marking capability built on multi-model orchestration - vision transformers for spatial understanding of handwritten layout, assessment-specific NLP models, weighted ensembles, and confidence scoring with anomaly detection that routes ambiguous regions to human review
- Displaces an entrenched manual workflow - the handwritten script evaluation market is currently dominated by labor-intensive manual marking processes, and Excelsoft's technology fundamentally displaces this workflow for examination boards, awarding bodies and educational institutions
- Responsible-AI framework treated as a commercial differentiator rather than compliance - explainable marking decisions, fairness audits for algorithmic bias across demographic groups, privacy by design, and detailed logs of all AI-powered decisions to meet the transparency and governance standards high-stakes assessment boards require
- Data custody as a trust moat - all customer data and assessment scripts remain within Excelsoft's secure, proprietary infrastructure; the Company does not train models on customer data without explicit consent, nor share assessment data with external AI providers
- Owned AI compute - an in-house GPU environment at Mysore (NVIDIA A6000 GPUs, NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada workstations, plus capacity at a peered partner data centre) lets customer workloads run on dedicated, ring-fenced environments and supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment for customers with strict data-residency obligations
- Proprietary internal AI leverage - Excelsoft GPT is fine-tuned on the Company's own codebase, technical documentation, domain knowledge and processes, so it provides significantly more valuable assistance than generic LLMs
- Engineering cost advantage - AI-assisted schema redesign delivered a 60% reduction in database footprint while maintaining or improving query performance, translating to lower infrastructure costs and improved scalability
- Long-tenured customer relationships - customers span more than 20 countries and many relationships have endured for over a decade, a durable switching-cost signal in high-stakes assessment
- Emerging high-margin AI service line - dedicated GPU hardware-as-a-service, managed model deployment and fine-tuning services position Excelsoft as a strategic AI partner rather than merely a SaaS vendor

- [AQA engagement] "A key highlight of the quarter has been the continued progress of our engagement with AQA. The implementation is advancing well, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner for delivering large-scale, mission-critical digital assessment solutions."
- [Labour Codes] The P&L shows an "Exceptional Item**" of Rs 6.72 Mn in Q4 FY26 with the footnote "**Exceptional Items is Impact of Labour Codes"; nil in Q1 FY27 and Q1 FY26.
- [Corporate status] Entity is "EXCELSOFT TECHNOLOGIES LIMITED, Formerly known as Excelsoft Technologies Private Limited", CIN L72900KA2000PLC027256, BSE Scrip Code 544617 / NSE symbol EXCELSOFT, ISIN INE606N01019, based at Hotagalli Industrial Area, Mysuru.
- [M&A history] Journey slide records acquisition of Freedom To Learn Limited as a wholly owned subsidiary (2008-11), acquisition of Meteor Online Learning Ltd. and incorporation of Excelsoft Technologies Inc. as a WOS (2014-18), and "Acquisition of Enhanzed Education Pvt. Ltd. as a WOS" (2022-25).
- [Leadership] CEO Doreswamy P is new to the role — "Co-Founder of CredoPay Technology Services Private Limited... will focus on driving growth and expansion as CEO"; CFO Poonacha Paruvangada was "Former Vice President - Finance, The India Cements Ltd.; CFO at United Breweries Ltd".

one-line thesis: Excelsoft delivered robust 29.5% YoY revenue growth in Q3FY26 driven by a 58% surge in EdTech services and landmark wins (Philippines Civil Services, VTCT UK), though reported margins compressed due to one-off M&A costs; the strategic pivot to recurring, licensable AI-platforms and active acquisition pipeline (US target in valuation stage) positions the company for accelerated scale despite near-term expense noise.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs.710mn (+29.5% YoY); EBITDA: Rs.197mn (+9.15% YoY), Margin: 27.7% (vs 32.8% YoY, impacted by Rs.29mn one-off legal/pro fees & labor code); PAT (Reported): Rs.103mn (+7.7% YoY); PAT (Normalized): Rs.133mn (+40% YoY, adj. for labor code); Order Book: Undisclosed but described as 'substantial' with recent landmark wins; Net Debt: Negative (Net Cash Rs.421cr). One-offs: Rs.29mn M&A advisory fees, Rs.40.7mn labor code impact.
guidance: No formal numerical guidance provided; Management indicates Q4 is seasonally strongest (~30% of annual revenue); Revenue from AQA partnership expected to start Q4FY26; Capex planned over 2 years for AI infrastructure upgrade.
order book & pipeline: Qualitatively 'substantial' with recent wins including Philippines Civil Services Commission (multi-year), VTCT UK (300k exams/year), and near-finalized AQA UK partnership; Top 10 customers contribute ~80% revenue with 11-year avg tenure.
segment / subsidiary detail: Q3 Revenue Mix: EdTech Services 65.7% (+58% YoY); Assessment & Proctoring 21%; Learning & Student Success 9.6%; Learning Design & Content 3.6%. 9M Revenue Mix: EdTech Services 57.5%; Assessment 26.4%.
growth verticals / optionality: Inorganic: Active diligence on US target (valuation stage) and UK targets to diversify geography; Organic: AI-enabled handwritten script marking (98.6% accuracy), expansion into vocational skills assessment, and deployment of 6 new AI/Quantum products.
margins & cost dynamics: Q3 EBITDA margin 27.7% vs 32.8% YoY; Normalized margin ~32% excluding Rs.29mn one-off M&A fees; Employee costs up 31.5% due to talent investment; Other expenses up 61% due to legal/pro fees and vendor costs.
capex / expansion: Plan to upgrade entire hardware stack to AI-enabled infrastructure (GPU farms, edge devices) over 2 years; Orders placed for modern cloud/GI devices; Funding available from IPO proceeds.
capital allocation: Net cash position of Rs.421cr; Released Rs.300cr corporate guarantee and Rs.165cr FD lien; Allocating capital towards strategic acquisitions (US/UK), AI infrastructure capex, and sales team expansion in US/ME/Singapore.
risks & watch-items: High client concentration (Top 5 = 72.2% revenue); Execution risk on large government contracts; Integration risk on pending acquisitions; Customer hesitation on AI ethics/adoption.
management quality / tone: Confident and aggressive on growth; Transparent on one-off costs; Emphasizes 'platform-led' transition over services; Cautious but active on M&A ('not going too bullish').
non-obvious takeaways: Company built proprietary multi-LLM stack achieving 98.6% accuracy on handwritten text extraction (vs industry 65-70%); Hiring retired industry consultants as lead generators in US/UK rather than just traditional sales hires; Fully on-premise AI data center approach for security vs cloud-native competitors.
